Recommending amendments to by law 8880, the private sewer and water service connection by law.
The recommended modifications are intended to provide payment options to residents that choose to replace their sewer line and bring the program more in line with the lead line replacement program.

More specifically, when replacing the public side of a residential sewer service and if the parallel water service to the property is non-led, the city will replace the sewer service only and leave the existing water service line.
In these cases, the property owner is offered an opportunity to replace the private side of the sewer service at the same time using the city's contractor.
Currently, residents choosing to replace the sewer service connection are only offered a one year deferral period.
If the owner, if the property owner opts out of replacing the private side, only the public side is then replaced.

The current by law only authorizes deferrals in situations where the city mandates replacement of a lead water service connection, in which case a property owner may be eligible to defer the costs of replacing the lead water line connection as well as the sewer connection if replaced concurrently.

The administration is recommending that the by law be updated to provide one three five and ten year deferral options for sewer only service connection replacements for residential property owners, which is consistent with the lead service line connection program.

Thanks again, Madam Chair. In January, Council approved in principle, a climate budget approach to be implemented for the 2024 2025 budget deliberations.
In addition, Council directed the administration to include carbon impacts for proposed capital projects with specific attention to impacts to the business as planned projection.

Given the significant effort and complexity to calculate greenhouse gases for all capital projects, the administration has developed criteria to propose which capital projects will undergo GHG quantification for the upcoming budget cycle.

The criteria that is being recommended includes projects with measurable GHG reductions, projects with measurable GHG additions resulting from implementation, and budgets with budgets of $2 million or greater.
Along with these criteria, the administration is recommending that only scope one and scope two emissions will be calculated.
So essentially this will not include emissions that occur outside this city boundary as a result of activities taking place within the city boundary.
For example, emissions embodied in fuels, water, food and construction materials will not be included.

Some examples of projects that would require GHG quantification are landfill optimization projects, renewable energy installations, road construction, park development and upgrades, new facilities and vehicles, bridge rehabilitation, water and wastewater treatment plant upgrades and electrical system distribution upgrades just to name a few.

If approved the next steps in the development of the climate budget will require amendments to the multi year business plan and budget policy for the climate budget to be developed and integrated into the financial business, sort of the financial budget book and for the departments responsible for capital projects to develop budget requests that include costs and GHG estimates.
